findings.title: Licensed and Qualified Environmental and Demolition Contractors
findings.fact: The City is seeking proposals from licensed and qualified environmental and demolition contractors.
findings.business_implication: Only contractors with appropriate licenses and qualifications in environmental abatement and demolition are eligible. This may limit competition but also ensures a certain level of expertise.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company holds all required licenses and certifications for environmental and demolition work in Rhode Island. If not, consider partnering with a qualified subcontractor or obtaining the necessary licenses before bidding.

quotes.quote: The City of Providence is seeking comprehensive, competitive proposals from licensed and qualified environmental and demolition contractors.

findings.title: Out-of-State Corporation Registration
findings.fact: Out-of-state corporations must qualify or register to transact business in Rhode Island.
findings.business_implication: If your company is incorporated outside Rhode Island, you must be registered to do business in the state before bidding. Failure to do so could disqualify your bid.
findings.action_recommendation: If you are an out-of-state corporation, ensure you are registered with the Rhode Island Secretary of State and have obtained a certificate of authority to transact business in the state. Include proof of registration in your bid package.

quotes.quote: A bidder who is an out-of-state corporation shall qualify or register to transact business in this State, in accordance with the Rhode Island Business Corporation Act, RIGL Sec. 7-1.2-1401, et seq.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Participation Goal
findings.fact: The City has a 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal, and bidders must submit MBE/WBE forms with their bid.
findings.business_implication: There is a 20% MBE/WBE participation goal. Bidders must either meet this goal or submit a waiver request. Failure to comply may affect bid evaluation or lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify certified MBE/WBE subcontractors or suppliers to meet the 20% goal. If unable to meet the goal, prepare a waiver request form and submit it to the MBE/WBE Outreach Director for approval before bid submission. Ensure all required forms are completed and included in the bid.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.

findings.title: Apprentice Requirements
findings.fact: Construction projects valued at $100,000 or more must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
findings.business_implication: This project likely exceeds $100,000, so the 15% apprentice hour requirement applies. Compliance is mandatory and must be reported with payment requisitions. Failure to meet this requirement could delay payments or result in penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to allocate at least 15% of total work hours to apprentices. Ensure you have access to qualified apprentices through registered apprenticeship programs. Prepare to track and report apprentice hours as required. Attend the mandatory meeting post-award to understand specific reporting procedures.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

findings.title: First Source Requirements
findings.fact: The project is subject to the City's First Source Ordinance, which requires hiring Providence residents.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must comply with local hiring requirements, which may affect labor costs and workforce planning. Non-compliance could lead to payment delays or penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the First Source Ordinance requirements, assess the availability of qualified Providence residents, and prepare a compliance plan. Ensure reporting mechanisms are in place to document hiring efforts.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.

findings.title: Proof of Licenses Required Before Award

findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to provide these documents quickly after being selected, or risk disqualification. This may require proactive gathering and verification of credentials.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required licenses, insurance certificates, and Certificate of Good Standing are current and readily accessible. Designate a point person to respond promptly to any requests from the issuing department.

quotes.quote: You must be able to provide: • Business Tax ID will be requested after an award is approved by the Board of Contract and Supply. • Proof of Insurance. • Certificate of Good Standing with the Rhode Island Secretary of State.

findings.title: Award to Lowest Qualified and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: Price is a critical factor, but you must also demonstrate that you are qualified and responsible. Simply being the lowest bidder does not guarantee the award.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your bid is competitive on price while also providing all required documentation and evidence of your qualifications, financial stability, and past performance.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Failure to Provide Supplemental Information May Lead to Disqualification
findings.fact: An inability to provide the outlined items at the request of the department may lead to the disqualification of your bid.
findings.business_implication: Even if you are the apparent low bidder, you must be able to provide requested supplemental information (e.g., tax ID, insurance, good standing certificate) upon request. Failure to do so can result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare these documents in advance so you can respond quickly if requested. Ensure your business is in good standing and you have the necessary insurance coverage.

quotes.quote: An inability to provide the outlined items at the request of the department may lead to the disqualification of your bid.

findings.title: Incomplete Bids May Be Disqualified
findings.fact: Failure to meet specified deadlines, follow specific submission instructions, or enclose all required documents with all applicable signatures will result in disqualification, or in an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.
findings.business_implication: Strict compliance with submission requirements is mandatory. Any missing document, missing signature, or failure to follow instructions can lead to immediate disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Use the bid package checklist to ensure all required forms are included, properly signed, and in the correct order. Double-check the submission method and deadline, and consider having a second person review the package before submission.

quotes.quote: Failure to meet specified deadlines, follow specific submission instructions, or enclose all required documents with all applicable signatures will result in disqualification, or in an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.

findings.title: Payment Terms: 60 Days
findings.fact: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will have to wait at least 60 days after invoice submission to receive payment, which could impact cash flow and require sufficient working capital to cover expenses during this period.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan cash flow accordingly, consider building the cost of delayed payment into pricing, and ensure all invoices include complete supporting documentation to avoid delays in the payment clock starting.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.

findings.title: Firm Prices for 90 Days
findings.fact: All bid prices will be considered firm for 90 days after bid opening, and requests for price increases will not be honored.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must maintain its quoted prices for at least 90 days after bid opening, even if material or labor costs increase during that period, which could erode profit margins if costs rise.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing includes a contingency for potential cost increases over the 90-day period, and avoid submitting bids with prices that are only viable for a shorter timeframe.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise. Requests for price increases will not be honored.

findings.title: No Assignment Without Consent
findings.fact: The contractor will not be permitted to assign or underlet the contract, or assign any monies or claims without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot transfer its rights or obligations under the contract to another party without the City's prior written consent, limiting flexibility in subcontracting or financing arrangements.
findings.action_recommendation: If the bidder anticipates needing to assign the contract or subcontract portions of the work, it should seek the City's consent in advance and ensure any subcontracts comply with this restriction.

quotes.quote: The contractor will NOT be permitted to: a) assign or underlet the contract, or b) assign either legally or equitably any monies or any claim thereto without the previous written consent of the City Purchasing Director.

findings.title: No Work Without Purchase Order
findings.fact: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must not begin performance or deliver goods until it receives a valid purchase order from the City, otherwise it risks non-payment or breach of contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Before starting any work or making deliveries, confirm that a purchase order has been issued and received; maintain clear communication with the City to ensure the purchase order is in place.

quotes.quote: No goods should be delivered, or work started without a Purchase Order.

findings.title: Prevailing Wage Requirement
findings.fact: Any construction over $1,000 is required by state law to pay state prevailing wage, and certified payrolls must be submitted before payments are made.
findings.business_implication: For construction projects exceeding $1,000, the bidder must pay prevailing wages as determined by state law and submit certified payrolls, which increases labor costs and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Incorporate prevailing wage rates into the bid pricing, ensure compliance with state wage determinations, and prepare to submit certified payrolls in a timely manner to avoid payment delays.

quotes.quote: Prevailing Wages: Any construction over $ 1,000.00 is required by state law to pay state prevailing wage.

All vendors supplying construction services must submit certified payrolls from any contractor and sub-contractor who work on the project. No payments are made until all payrolls are up to date, and correct.

findings.title: Unlimited Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: Contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City and its officials from all claims, damages, losses, and expenses arising out of the work, with no stated limit.
findings.business_implication: This clause exposes the contractor to potentially unlimited financial liability, including legal fees and damages, for any claims arising from the work, even if caused by the City's own negligence. This could significantly impact profitability and solvency.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek to negotiate a cap on indemnification obligations, such as limiting to the contract value or to the extent of the contractor's negligence. Also, ensure adequate insurance coverage, including professional liability and umbrella policies, to mitigate potential exposure.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: No Limitation of Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit, and the City has the full statute of limitations to bring claims.
findings.business_implication: The contractor's liability is uncapped, meaning a single claim could exceed the contract value and potentially bankrupt the business. The extended statute of limitations also prolongs the period of risk exposure.
findings.action_recommendation: Attempt to negotiate a mutual waiver of consequential damages and a cap on total liability, such as the contract price or a multiple thereof. Also, consider purchasing higher limits of liability insurance and discuss with legal counsel the implications of the extended claims period.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements and Additional Insured
findings.fact: Contractor must maintain insurance coverage and name the City as an additional insured on general liability and umbrella policies.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must secure and maintain specific insurance policies, which may increase costs. Naming the City as an additional insured extends coverage to the City, potentially increasing premiums and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current insurance policies to ensure they meet the requirements and that the City can be added as an additional insured. Obtain quotes for additional insured endorsements and factor these costs into the bid. Ensure compliance with all insurance obligations to avoid default.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Payments
findings.fact: The City is not obligated to pay interest on overdue invoices or any costs associated with collection.
findings.business_implication: The contractor will not receive compensation for late payments, which can strain cash flow and increase the cost of borrowing. The contractor also bears the risk of collection costs if the City fails to pay.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor the cost of delayed payments into the pricing. Consider negotiating for a shorter payment term or a provision for interest on late payments. Maintain clear invoicing procedures and follow up promptly on overdue invoices to minimize delays.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment. In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: No Dispute Resolution or Arbitration
findings.fact: The City is not required to submit to dispute resolution or binding arbitration; disputes may only be resolved in court.
findings.business_implication: Disputes must be resolved through litigation, which is typically more time-consuming and costly than arbitration. The contractor may face significant legal expenses and delays in resolving conflicts.
findings.action_recommendation: Consider the potential for disputes and the cost of litigation when pricing the contract. Explore the possibility of negotiating a binding arbitration clause or at least a structured negotiation process. Ensure all contractual obligations are meticulously documented to minimize disputes.

quotes.quote: With regard to any issues, claims, or controversies that may arise under this Agreement, the City shall not be required to submit to dispute resolution or mandatory/binding arbitration. Nothing prevents the parties from mutually agreeing to settle any disputes using mediation or non-binding arbitration.

findings.title: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
findings.fact: The agreement is governed by Rhode Island law, and all actions must be brought in Rhode Island state or federal court.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to litigate any disputes in Rhode Island, which may be inconvenient and costly if the bidder is located outside the state. It also means Rhode Island law will apply, potentially differing from the bidder's home state laws.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the feasibility of accepting Rhode Island jurisdiction and consider the potential legal costs. If acceptable, ensure internal legal counsel is aware. If not, consider negotiating this term or factoring the risk into the bid price.

quotes.quote: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Rhode Island. You expressly submit yourself to and agree that any and all actions arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the Agreement or relationship between the parties shall occur solely in the venue and jurisdiction of the State of Rhode Island or the federal court located in Rhode Island.

findings.title: Data Breach Notification Obligation
findings.fact: Contractor must notify the City within 24 hours of a breach of confidential or personal information and implement security measures.
findings.business_implication: The 24-hour notification requirement is extremely tight and may be difficult to meet, especially if the breach is discovered outside business hours. Non-compliance could lead to contractual penalties or damage to reputation. The requirement to implement security measures may impose additional costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that incident response procedures are in place to detect and report breaches within 24 hours. Review current security measures to ensure they meet the contract's requirements. Consider including a provision for notification to be made as soon as possible but no later than 24 hours, and clarify the definition of 'breach' to avoid ambiguity.

quotes.quote: In the event of a breach of such information, you shall notify the City of such breach immediately, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after discovery of such breach.

findings.title: Default for Failure to Deliver or Meet Specifications
findings.fact: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.
findings.business_implication: The bidder faces the risk of being declared in default if they fail to meet delivery deadlines or specifications, which could lead to termination, financial penalties, or negative impact on future bids. This is a high-risk area as project delays or quality issues can occur.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the delivery schedule and specifications to ensure they are realistic and achievable. Develop a robust project management plan to mitigate risks of delay or non-compliance. If there are concerns about meeting the schedule, consider submitting a bid with a longer timeline or clarifying any ambiguities in the specifications before bidding.

quotes.quote: Failure to deliver within the time quoted or failure to meet specifications may result in default in accordance with the general specifications.

findings.title: Conflicting Bid Due Dates: Page 13 vs. Page 5
findings.fact: Page 13 states bids are due Monday, July 27, 2026, while page 5 states awards will be made within 90 days of bid opening, but the bid opening date is not specified. The 90-day period may conflict with the project schedule.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity regarding the bid opening date and the 90-day award period could lead to uncertainty about the project timeline. If the bid opening is not clearly defined, the 90-day period may start later than expected, potentially delaying the project start and affecting the bidder's resource allocation.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the City regarding the exact bid opening date and how the 90-day award period will be calculated. This will help in planning resources and understanding the expected timeline. If no clarification is provided, assume the worst-case scenario and plan accordingly.

quotes.quote: Bids Due  Monday, July 27, 2026
Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening.

findings.title: Ambiguity in Bid Package Requirements: Page 3 vs. Page 14
findings.fact: Page 3 lists required documents for the bid package, while page 14 states that certain items (Business Tax ID, Proof of Insurance, Certificate of Good Standing) are NOT required in the initial bid but may be requested later. This could be seen as contradictory regarding what must be submitted initially.
findings.business_implication: The contradiction could lead to confusion about what documents are mandatory for the initial bid. If the bidder omits items that are actually required, they risk disqualification. Conversely, including unnecessary documents may not be harmful but could be seen as non-compliance with instructions.
findings.action_recommendation: To avoid disqualification, include all documents listed on page 3 in the initial bid, as they are explicitly required. Additionally, be prepared to provide the items listed on page 14 upon request after the award. If there is any doubt, seek clarification from the City before submitting the bid.

quotes.quote: All of the above listed documents are REQUIRED. (With the exception of financial assurances, which are only required if specified on page 5.)
This information is NOT requested to be provided in your initial bid that you will submit to the City Clerk’s office by the “date to be opened” noted on page 1.
